stories.headline: GVMC Mayor post reserved for women as Visakhapatnam prepares for first direct mayoral election in 26 years
stories.title: GVMC Mayor post reserved for women as Visakhapatnam prepares for first direct mayoral election in 26 years
stories.summary: The last direct election was in 2000, when Rajana Ramani won under the Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation; TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Rao says water supply would be the alliance’s priority
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Political activity in the city has picked up following the Andhra Pradesh government’s release of G.O. Ms. No. 252, which finalises the reservation categories for the posts of Mayor in the State’s 17 municipal corporations, including the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) here.
Issued by Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar on Monday (October 12, 2026), the notification reserves the GVMC Mayor post for Women (General).
The upcoming civic polls follow a major change in local body governance enacted by the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly through the Municipal Laws (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2026.

The legislation restored the direct election of Mayors and Chairpersons of urban local bodies for a fixed five-year term, reversing the indirect election model that had been in place since August 2005.
In 2000, Rajana Ramani won the Mayor’s seat in a direct (public vote) election under the previous Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (VMC).

This was the last direct mayoral election held in the city for over two decades, as subsequent elections (following the city’s upgrade to the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation) shifted to the indirect system.
Golagani Hari Venkata Kumari won the seat in the indirect voting system.
“This format marks the return of direct mayoral elections to Visakhapatnam after 26 years.
The last direct election was held in 2000 when the body was under the Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation.
Rajana Ramani was the Mayor then.
If our alliance parties win, our top priority would be the water supply to the city,” Gajuwaka MLA and TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Rao told.
The Hindu.

stories.headline: Monocracy In Election Commission: Testing Statutory Consensus Under 2023 CEC Act
stories.title: Monocracy In Election Commission: Testing Statutory Consensus Under 2023 CEC Act
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A Public Interest Litigation filed in the Supreme Court on September 25, 2026, by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi has brought an unprecedented internal rift within the Election Commission of India into the judicial spotlight.

It seeks the initiation of criminal proceedings against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, as well as a probe into the alleged unilateral orders of the CEC by forming a Special Investigation Team.

As per Indian Express expose, fourteen formal written objections to the Chief Election Commissioner's executive orders by the Election Commissioners Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Dr. Vivek Joshi were documented over a period of ten months, which cannot be dismissed as routine administrative friction.

The internal breach regarding the Chief Election Commissioner's unilateral executive orders without collective decision-making, the modification of voter registration rules via updates to digital portals, and the centralization of electoral rolls management in Delhi represent direct violations of multi-member decision-making obligations per the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

The Election Commission's official defense, issued on September 23, 2026, and reiterated following an all-member meeting on September 26, 2026, that written notes merely reflect standard internal deliberation fails statutory scrutiny.
In T.N. Seshan.

Union of India, the Supreme Court unambiguously denied the possibility of the existence of a supreme Chief Election Commissioner, as the statutory scheme was purposefully devised to prevent arbitrary executive governance.
The violation of this results in transforming the internal dispute into administrative illegality.
Multi-Member Governance or Monocratic Rule?
The statutory framework governing the internal decision-making process is established in Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.
Per Section 18(2), the Commission shall transact its business unanimously.
Where there is a difference of opinion between the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners, then the matter will be decided according to the opinion of the majority.

stories.headline: "We will never go back to square one": Iran remains open to US nuclear talks with firm conditions
stories.title: "We will never go back to square one": Iran remains open to US nuclear talks with firm conditions
stories.summary: Tehran [Iran], October 12 : In a definitive declaration outlining Tehran’s diplomatic stance, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei asserted that while Iran is willing to engage in nuclear negotiations with the United States, it will not reset the clock on past grievances or ignore the changing realities on the ground. Speaking on Monday against the backdrop of heightened Middle East tensions and ongoing economic sanctions, Baghaei firmly rejected the idea that diplomacy can simply return to its original baseline. "We will never go back to square one. Can you ignore the experiences of the past two years and then say that we are back to square one? Every day that passes, we will definitely use its experience, both in terms of strengthening our own capabilities and in terms of learning from the other side’s lapses," he said. Baghaei emphasised that Tehran has not walked away from the negotiating table, framing diplomacy as an integral tool alongside national defence. "We are so confident that we will never run away from the negotiating table and diplomacy. Diplomacy is as important to us as the battlefield and war. We will definitely use the tools of diplomacy, wherever necessary and wherever possible, to secure our interests," said Baghaei. However, he pointed out a direct contradiction in Western strategy, arguing that military pressure, sanctions, and economic warfare undermine the genuine spirit of negotiations. "The party that should be solely blamed and held accountable for this situation is the party that destroyed the negotiating table in the middle of the negotiations and continues to insist on its previous excesses. How can one claim to negotiate and be diplomatic, while they have escalated the economic war, have practically maintained the conditions of war, and then claim that they are seeking negotiations?" questioned Baghaei. Addressing Western anxieties over Iran’s potential departure from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), Baghaei noted that international inaction following attacks on Iranian peaceful nuclear infrastructure has fueled debate within the country. "Why are they worried? There is no point in worrying. They have created this concern themselves. Self-inflicted is not a tactic," he said. He added that those responsible for undermining global non-proliferation norms must be held accountable. "Those who themselves have caused the weakening of the foundations of the non-proliferation regime must answer this question; not only in Iran, but in the entire region and globally," said Baghaei. Responding to reports that the pre-war "Cairo Agreement", a framework negotiated between Iran's Foreign Minister and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) chief, could serve as a roadmap to break the deadlock, Baghaei signalled that the window for that arrangement had closed. "The Cairo Agreement, which is now part of history, the opposing parties did not really appreciate its opportunity," said Baghaei. Regarding third-party mediation, while Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed the Iranian nuclear situation with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and subsequently US President Donald Trump, Baghaei reiterated the established official channels for US-Iran communications. "We have always welcomed the wonderful efforts of friendly countries; But as you know, technically and in the strict sense of the word, Pakistan and Qatar continue to play the role of mediator between Iran and the United States," added Baghaei. The spokesperson's remarks follow parallel political developments. Russian President Vladimir Putin stressed during discussions that "the scope for diplomacy on Iran is far from exhausted" and called an agreement both possible and necessary. US President Donald Trump noted that the conflict with Iran would conclude "very soon," either through continued military pressure or an agreement on Washington's terms, reiterating that "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon". Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei stated that while the US addressed some of Iran's seven conditions regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, Washington's overall response remained "inadequate". (ANI)

A standing order issued on October 11 by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar named Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as the new designated sites for protests and demonstrations. "They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it's no a longer protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!," Dipke said in a post on X. In another post, Dipke said Prime Minister Narendra Modi could "denotify democracy" next. "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself. The dictator's problem was never the protest site. It was the very idea of people protesting," Dipke said on social media.

stories.headline: Neither approved nor rejected ECI's new Form 6, clarifies Supreme Court
stories.title: Neither approved nor rejected ECI's new Form 6, clarifies Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had not adjudicated on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) modified Form 6 declaration for new voter registration, observing that the revised form was not before it when it decided the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls case.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had not adjudicated on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) modified Form 6 declaration for new voter registration, observing that the revised form was not before it when it decided the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls case.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had not adjudicated on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) modified Form 6 declaration for new voter registration, observing that the revised form was not before it when it decided the Bihar Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls case.

A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the clarification while hearing a fresh petition raising concerns over the functioning of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the changes to Form 6, which requires applicants seeking registration as new voters to disclose whether they or their parents were mapped in the previous SIR.

During the hearing, counsel for the petitioner submitted that the Supreme Court had clarified on October 5 that the modified Form 6 had not been approved by it, while the ECI had claimed that the revised declaration had received the top court’s approval.

Responding to the submission, Justice Bagchi said the Supreme Court had not adjudicated on the new Form 6, adding that the revised form was not in existence when the judgment in the Bihar SIR case was delivered.
"There is no adjudication on the new Form 6," he observed, clarifying that the apex court’s earlier oral remarks could not be construed as either approving or disapproving the modified declaration.
CJI Surya Kant cautioned against selectively interpreting the top court’s observations for media reports, saying: "Please don’t pick words for news items."

The clarification comes amid a political row over the modified Form 6 declaration, with questions being raised about the circumstances in which the changes were introduced and whether they were implemented despite objections from two Election Commissioners.

The controversy intensified after the ECI issued a press release on September 26 suggesting that the Supreme Court had upheld the revised declaration in its May 2026 judgment concerning the Bihar SIR exercise.
However, the modified declaration was introduced after the judgment, and the Supreme Court had no occasion to examine its contents while deciding the Bihar SIR matter.
Under the revised declaration, applicants seeking registration as new voters are required to state whether they or their parents were included in the previous SIR.
The earlier version of Form 6 used during the SIR exercise in other states did not contain this requirement.

stories.headline: Madhur Bhandarkar to lead Feature Film jury at 57th Indian Panorama
stories.title: Madhur Bhandarkar to lead Feature Film jury at 57th Indian Panorama
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 12 : Filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar, who is known for ‘Chandni Bar’, ‘Page 3’, ‘Fashion’, and ‘Babli Bouncer’, has been appointed as the Chairman of the Jury for the Feature Film Section of Indian Panorama for the upcoming 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. As Chairman of the Feature Film Jury, he will be responsible for evaluating eligible entries and recommending 25 outstanding feature films for showcase at the 57th IFFI. This selection will include five films from mainstream cinema recommended by designated film trade bodies. The festival primarily comprises two major sections, International Cinema and Indian Panorama. The Indian Panorama is a flagship section dedicated to showcasing the best of contemporary Indian cinema and promoting excellence in filmmaking. The official communication was issued by Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director of the 57th IFFI. The film festival, which is organised by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, the International Film Festival of India has been celebrating cinema from across the world since its inception in 1952. From the selected films, the jury will recommend three films for the main competition, two films for the Best Debut Film of a Director category, and three films for the ICFT UNESCO-Gandhi Medal under the international competition. The jury will also evaluate entries for the Best Debut Director of Indian Feature Film Award, recommending five films and selecting the winner. The primary jury screening of eligible feature film entries commenced online on September 29 and is scheduled to continue until October 16, 2026. This will be followed by the central panel jury screening of 60 shortlisted feature films at the NFDC Auditorium in Mumbai from October 18 to November 1, 2026. The 57th edition of IFFI is set to be held from November 20 to November 28, 2026 in Goa. --IANS

stories.title: Put Your GDP Growth Next to Ours! | Piyush Goyal on Why India Will Double Its Economy Every 8 Years
stories.summary: Speaking at The Dilli Dialogue in New Delhi, Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal broke down India’s fearless economic pitch to the world. Highlighting India’s purchasing power parity of nearly $16 to $19 trillion, Goyal revealed his direct challenge to global trade ministers: while aging developed economies struggle to even double their size, India’s young, skilled workforce is set to double the nation's GDP every eight years on the road to a $30 trillion economy by 2047. From German factories seeking 90,000 workers annually to Japan’s demand for 300,000 skilled professionals, Goyal explained why Indian talent, work ethic, and family values provide an unmatched competitive edge on the global stage.

stories.title: NHRC has grown into trusted address for aggrieved, says CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday said the NHRC has grown into a "trusted address" for the aggrieved and the true measure of a human rights institution is not only the number of cases it decides, but whether it can be heard by those who are least able to make themselves heard. The CJI was speaking at the 33rd Foundation Day function of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) at Vigyan Bhawan here. "Thirty-three years ago, Parliament created this Commission to stand guard over human dignity. In the years since, it has grown from a new idea into a trusted address for the aggrieved," he said. "If the Constitution is the promise, the Commission is one of its keepers. It goes where the court cannot easily go; it listens to those who cannot easily speak, and it can act on its own without waiting to be asked," the CJI said. Referring to the NHRC's interventions in cases involving custodial torture or deaths, bonded labour, industrial exposure to silicosis and protectio

stories.headline: Jantar Mantar de-notified as protest site; Delhi Police designates 3 new venues
stories.title: Jantar Mantar de-notified as protest site; Delhi Police designates 3 new venues
stories.summary: New Delhi , Oct 12 : Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated venue for organising protests and demonstrations in Delhi, with the Delhi Police designating three new locations for the purpose, according to an official notice. The three new designated protest venues are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations in place of the existing designated site. Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a protest venue, the notice stated. Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar said that a detailed and revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for organising protests and demonstrations at the three designated venues would be issued separately. The notice partially modifies the earlier Standing Order dated April 28, 2022. The revised SOP is expected to lay down the procedures for organising protests and demonstrations at the newly designated venues. The development comes as leaders and parliamentarians of the opposition INDIA bloc launched a massive protest march from Connaught Place in central Delhi, intensifying their agitation against the Election Commission over alleged electoral manipulation and subversion of democratic institutions. Launching a fierce attack on the central government during the march, Congress General Secretary (Organisation) KC Venugopal described the Opposition's ongoing agitation as the "biggest andolan" against the poll panel and declared that the party is taking its legal battle to the apex court. "This is the biggest andolan against the Election Commissioner and the election system. Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are using the Chief Election Commissioner as their tool to destroy the democracy of this country, to hijack the democracy of the country," Venugopal said. Emphasizing that the Opposition will fight on both political and legal fronts, he said, "Therefore, for the last one week, we are on the streets. Today also we are going to be on the streets, and we are going to file a petition in the Supreme Court also." When asked by reporters regarding an appointment with the Chief Justice of India, Venugopal stated, "I don't want to comment on all that now. But anyway, we are going to fight legally also. We are going to the Supreme Court and file a petition there. The Supreme Court, Chief Justice informed us that between 10:00 to 4:00, they are ready to receive our petition; the registry is ready." Joining the protest, Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury condemned the police clampdown and accused the government of acting with impunity despite judicial safeguards. "This is a show of giving them assurance that we are going to fight for them, that we represent them and their voice should be heard here. This brute force here and declaring us unlawful is a clear show of violation of anything that is constitutional and disrespect to the Supreme Court which this government is showing," Chowdhury said. She added, "Despite the Supreme Court's rulings, they have violated and they have named us. You ask about SIR and they filed an FIR. One Gyanesh is more than 'Bharat desh'?" Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee said, "We are demanding justice, nothing else. This is for people, for humankind, for justice...We want justice and nothing else." Against this backdrop, high security is in place in Central Delhi with barricades at multiple locations. Entry and exit at certain metro stations will also remain closed from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM on October 12, 2026, for security reasons. The stations are Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat, Barakhamba Road respectively. Security personnel have been deployed at Barakhamba Road, near Mandi House. RAF (Rapid Action Force) and CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force) personnel are also deployed along with Delhi Police personnel.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On PIL Seeking Proper Maintenance Of Accessible Airport Infrastructure
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On PIL Seeking Proper Maintenance Of Accessible Airport Infrastructure
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice on a PIL seeking proper maintenance of accessible airport infrastructure, including tactile pathways, Braille signage, accessible seating, and priority check-in for persons with disabilities.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana called for the responses of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, the Airport Authority of India, the Central Industrial Security Force and the Digi Yatra Foundation.

The public interest litigation, filed by one Turab Chimthanawala, challenges "systemic and continuing failure" on the part of respondent-authorities in ensuring and operationalizing the accessibility standards and regulatory mandates governing civil aviation in India, including the Accessibility Standards and Guidelines for Civil Aviation 2022, Rule 15(1)(f) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules 2017, the Civil Aviation Requirements titled "Carriage by Air-Persons with Disability (Divyangjan) and/or Persons with Reduced Mobility" (PRM-CAR) issued by the DGCA.

He claims that despite a comprehensive statutory and regulatory framework, there is complete absence of a proper monitoring mechanism that would ensure implementation of the 2022 Standards and Guidelines and the PRM-CAR.

"This systemic failure has resulted in continuing and widespread inaccessibility across civil aviation infrastructure and services, including inaccessible airport infrastructure, lack of accessible signage and navigation systems, absence of accessible digital and biometric systems such as DigiYatra, inaccessible booking and check-in systems, improper handling of mobility aids, lack of trained personnel, coercive or inappropriate assistance practices, and the absence of dignified and accessible screening and immigration procedures.
These failures constitute a continuing violation of statutory mandates as well as the fundamental rights of PwDs."
The petitioner seeks enforcement of fundamental rights of persons with disabilities, including their Right to Accessibility, an integral part of Articles 14, 19(1)(d) and 21 of the Constitution.
He avers that the State and its instrumentalities have a "non-derogable obligation" to ensure that public infrastructure and services are usable by PwDs on an equal basis with others.
The petition has been drawn by Advocates Rahul Bajaj, Amar Jain, Sarah and Amritesh Mishra, and filed through AoR Ashutosh Senger.

stories.headline: Supreme Court urged to list contempt plea urgently over alleged release of GM rice
stories.title: Supreme Court urged to list contempt plea urgently over alleged release of GM rice
stories.summary: Lawyer Prashant Bhushan informed the SC bench that approval for cultivating herbicide-tolerant GM basmati rice has been granted, and the contempt plea should be heard soon.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court was on Monday urged to urgently list contempt petitions alleging violation of its 2024 judgment on genetically modified (GM) crops, amid concerns over the alleged approval for the cultivation of herbicide-tolerant GM basmati rice.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told by lawyer Prashant Bhushan that now, the approval for cultivation of herbicide-tolerant GM basmati rice has been given and hence the contempt plea be heard as early as possible.
The lawyer referred to the 2024 judgment delivered by a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and Sanjay Karol, which had a split verdict on one issue that was referred to a larger bench.
He said the contempt petitions arose from the common judgment and were unrelated to the reference concerning GM mustard, which was listed before a special three-judge bench.
"The contempt petitions are not related to the reference.
They arise out of the common judgment of the court.
They can be listed before the regular contempt bench," Bhushan submitted.
He said the contempt petition, filed in 2025, had not been taken up despite being mentioned earlier.
According to him, the special bench hearing the GM mustard reference had declined to hear the contempt petitions.
"They have now given the go-ahead to plant genetically modified basmati rice, which is a herbicide-tolerant variety.
It will destroy our basmati.
It will contaminate and cause havoc," Bhushan said, urging the court to list the matter at the earliest.

stories.headline: Saikia denies reports of India-Sri Lanka ODI shifting to Ahmedabad
stories.title: Saikia denies reports of India-Sri Lanka ODI shifting to Ahmedabad
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 12 : BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia on Monday denied reports claiming that the first ODI between India and Sri Lanka, originally scheduled to be held in the national capital on December 13, has been moved to Ahmedabad. The clarification comes amid reports regarding the non-availability of the Arun Jaitley Stadium, where the Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) is currently undertaking major infrastructure overhauls, including the installation of a modern drainage system along with the relaying of pitches and outfield. “Reports suggesting that the India–Sri Lanka ODI match scheduled in Delhi may be shifted to Ahmedabad are not accurate. There has been no such decision (taken) by the BCCI. “We request media colleagues to kindly refer to official BCCI communications for any updates regarding the schedule. Further, it needs to be reiterated that bilateral matches are primarily allotted by following a standard policy," said Saikia in a statement on Monday. IANS had previously reported on September 25 that the major overhaul of the drainage system at the stadium had led to Delhi’s home games in Elite Group C of the Ranji Trophy 2026/27 being shifted to the Air Force Ground in Palam. Interestingly, the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad is already scheduled to host the third India-Sri Lanka ODI on December 19, after the second game takes place at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru on December 16. The ODI matches are of immense importance to India, the two-time champions, in terms of building up and fine-tuning their combinations for the 2027 Men’s ODI World Cup, to be played in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. India batting stalwart and former skipper Virat Kohli, who was a member of the 2011 edition winning team on home soil, had previously said to broadcasters JioStar that the mega event in 2027 would be his last appearance for India in a World Cup. --IANS

stories.headline: Turning interest into fandom is our goal for women’s football: Jinisha Sharma
stories.title: Turning interest into fandom is our goal for women’s football: Jinisha Sharma
stories.summary: Of all the shenanigans Rebecca Welton pulls off in Ted Lasso, the much-feted American TV series about the fictional English football club AFC Richmond, nothing compares to her audacious bet in the recently concluded final season: Launching a women’s team against conventional wisdom and financial prudence. Jinisha Sharma, director of Capri Sports, the sports development arm of NBFC Capri Global, has watched the series too and knows all too well that the task she has taken on will require far more guts and gusto than Welton’s.Last month, Capri Sports, which also owns the franchise UP Warriorz (UPW) in the Women’s Premier League (WPL), signed a 15-year contract with the All India Football Federation (AIFF) to market and commercially develop the top two tiers of India’s national women’s football league—the Indian Women’s League (IWL) and IWL 2. Why has Capri chosen to invest in the women’s game, which has little visibility and following in the country? Sharma explains in a conversation with Forbes India. Edited excerpts:Q. Fifteen years is a long commitment in a sport that hasn’t yet had much commercial success. What convinced you to take the bet?At Capri Sports, we have been talking a lot about investing in women's sports. The contours of that include both where that is going to lead to a podium finish as well as where that is going to lead to commercial prowess. We have been evaluating multiple opportunities for quite some time to see where we can have a long-term impact, and women’s football has been on our mind from the very early days. This isn’t a decision we have taken just today, but years ago, when we started to evaluate which sports are primed for commercial success.Q. But women’s football doesn’t quite have that visibility yet.In sports, especially in women's sports, the connection needs to come from the audience. And we're hoping to bring in more young girls and women who become sports fans.One of the most important aspects of that continues to be their personal relationship with the sport. Our country has an incredible number of schools that offer an opportunity to play football, which means a lot of young girls have been exposed to football. In pop culture, too, they have consumed enough and more stories about the sport. Our bet has been based on our understanding of how we will be able to convert that association with a sport into its fandom. We are hoping IWL will be the missing link where girls who play football will also be able to watch it.We have seen that arc with the UP Warriorz (UPW) in the Women’s Premier League (WPL), where young girls and women are now starting to connect to cricket more deeply. We think this journey will be faster in football because a large number of young girls are into football already.And our investment in women’s football doesn’t start with the IWL. opening: Of all the shenanigans Rebecca Welton pulls off in Ted Lasso, the much-feted American TV series about the fictional English football club AFC Richmond, nothing compares to her audacious bet in the recently concluded final season: Launching a women’s team against conventional wisdom and financial prudence.

Jinisha Sharma, director of Capri Sports, the sports development arm of NBFC Capri Global, has watched the series too and knows all too well that the task she has taken on will require far more guts and gusto than Welton’s.
body: Last month, Capri Sports, which also owns the franchise UP Warriorz (UPW) in the Women’s Premier League (WPL), signed a 15-year contract with the All India Football Federation (AIFF) to market and commercially develop the top two tiers of India’s national women’s football league—the Indian Women’s League (IWL) and IWL 2.
Why has Capri chosen to invest in the women’s game, which has little visibility and following in the country?
Sharma explains in a conversation with Forbes India.
Edited excerpts:Q. Fifteen years is a long commitment in a sport that hasn’t yet had much commercial success.
What convinced you to take the bet?
At Capri Sports, we have been talking a lot about investing in women's sports.
The contours of that include both where that is going to lead to a podium finish as well as where that is going to lead to commercial prowess.
We have been evaluating multiple opportunities for quite some time to see where we can have a long-term impact, and women’s football has been on our mind from the very early days.

This isn’t a decision we have taken just today, but years ago, when we started to evaluate which sports are primed for commercial success.Q. But women’s football doesn’t quite have that visibility yet.
In sports, especially in women's sports, the connection needs to come from the audience.
And we're hoping to bring in more young girls and women who become sports fans.
Our country has an incredible number of schools that offer an opportunity to play football, which means a lot of young girls have been exposed to football.
In pop culture, too, they have consumed enough and more stories about the sport.
Our bet has been based on our understanding of how we will be able to convert that association with a sport into its fandom.
We are hoping IWL will be the missing link where girls who play football will also be able to watch it.
We have seen that arc with the UP Warriorz (UPW) in the Women’s Premier League (WPL), where young girls and women are now starting to connect to cricket more deeply.
We think this journey will be faster in football because a large number of young girls are into football already.
And our investment in women’s football doesn’t start with the IWL.
We have two initiatives prior to that—Warriorz FC, a senior district-level football team that Capri Sports owns in Mumbai, and Nova Sports, a football development pathway for girls..
But converting fandom might not automatically make a sports property a successful business.
We have seen that with men’s football, which has an enormous following in India.
Which is exactly why we have made the 15-year bet.
We know there is a lot to do.
None of us is saying that everything that we're imagining will happen right from the get-go.
But we're hoping that bringing in a platform like this will enable more structure within women's football and lead to bigger moments.
We've seen that, with far lesser investment and visibility, a far greater attempt at qualification at the AFC level is possible.
So we see a lot of opportunity to drive commercial success with this.

Apart from the WPL, we really feel football is another sport that can capture large audiences with a healthy female ratio.Q. Earlier, you spoke about how you have been evaluating this proposition for quite some time.
What have you seen through that evaluation?
One of the early markers for us, of course, was our journey with Warriorz FC, a senior district-level football team that Capri Sports owns in Mumbai.
It helped us understand what the realities of women’s football are.
We are not going into this doe-eyed and unaware of the challenges.
One of the early things we have uncovered is that there is a lot of talent and a lot of interest among girls in playing.
Between June 2022 and March 2024, the number of registered women footballers jumped from 11,724 to 27,936—that’s over 138 percent.
But there is no clear pathway.
If a girl starts playing football at eight, nine or ten, where does she go after that?
Plus, there is a lack of access to structured training and consistent competition.
So you don’t know where the long-term opportunities are.
Warriorz FC gave us an understanding of what we need to solve for.Q. India is now a land of leagues.
What do some of these leagues teach you about building another from scratch?
Looking at both leagues that have done well and those that haven’t has helped us understand unit economics—how we need to invest the right amount and not overspend.

Some of the early conversations we had with advisors who have worked on crafting leagues globally told us not to overinflate the proposition—let’s not try to position the league as the best ever, so don’t overpackage.

While these are the two topmost tiers of women’s football, there are still realities like the quality of the grounds that they play on and the fact that clubs are still struggling, etc. We are hoping that the league will be able to grow gradually in such a manner that it will create recognition in the market and a connection with the audience.
At the moment, we are focusing on making sure we produce it well so that the audience watching it for the first time will want to invest more time in the subsequent edition.
We are debating whether we should refrain from going too wide in the funnel and making it a mass property.
Is it more important to make the game more accessible or to build commercial value from Day 1—an example would be whether you want to put it behind a paywall?
And most importantly, we need to build the storytelling through clubs, players and rivalries.
The IWL started in 2016, but few people know about it.
We will share whatever resources we have to help the clubs understand what to make of this opportunity.
Most IWL club owners come from a place of passion, and we respect that deeply.
We have to ensure this is now seen from the lens of growth as well..
Any templates from successful women’s leagues globally that you are looking to follow?
There are two that we always speak about internally—the WSL in the UK and the NWSL in the US.
They have given us a really good blueprint in the way they invest in match-day rituals to build fans.
These are largely things that the clubs have done, but there are definitely learnings at a league level.
We are here for 15 years, so we have to invest in the people.
You just saw the passion for the game during the recent India-Brazil [friendly].
That needs to be tapped into.
And, for that, the biggest thing that we have to do right now is build awareness.
For instance, there are three clubs from Delhi in this year’s IWL—how incredible would it be to involve the city’s community and encourage some soccer rivalry?
Internally, our discussion today isn’t about making it the biggest viewership property from day one.
I want to make sure that I'm getting depth from the people who already care about football.
And a lot of our conversations with fans have shown us that it’s got nothing to do with male or female fans—they just care about the game.
Our conversations with fans have shown us that they care about the game, regardless of gender.
So, our markers have shown that there is a lot of interest; now it's really our job to make sure that it sustains and then converts into fandom.Q. So, where do you start?
What’s the first thing on your agenda?
IWL 2 is really right upon us—it’s starting later this month.
We've not really had much time with that.
I am just focused on making sure that we're able to get all the systems in place for that.
For IWL, of course, we are looking to ensure that the process to build the fan base gets started.
